The crew is selected from the following list, which specifies exactly the tasks each person can do: George: taping Helena: sanding, priming Inga: framing, priming Kelly: framing, sanding Leanda: wallboarding, taping Maricita: sanding Olaf: wallboarding, priming The following conditions must apply: At least one task is done each day. Taping and priming are done on different days. Each crew member does at least one task during the installation, but no more than one task a day. Each task is done by exactly one worker, completed the day it is started and before the next task begins.
question: Which one of the following could be a pair of members of the crew both of whom work on the same days as each other and each of whom perform two tasks?
options: A) George and Maricita
B) Helena and Kelly
C) Inga and Leanda
D) Kelly and Leanda
E) Leanda and Olaf

# Declarations
workers = EnumSort([George, Helena, Inga, Kelly, Leanda, Maricita, Olaf])
tasks = EnumSort([framing, wallboarding, taping, sanding, priming])
assign = Function([workers, tasks] -> [bool])

# Constraints
ForAll([w:workers], Exists([t:tasks], assign(w, t))) ::: Each crew member does at least one task
ForAll([w:workers], ForAll([t1:tasks, t2:tasks], Implies(t1 != t2, Not(And(assign(w, t1), assign(w, t2))))) ::: Each crew member does no more than one task per day
ForAll([t:tasks], Exists([w:workers], assign(w, t))) ::: Each task is done by exactly one worker
ForAll([w:workers], ForAll([d:tasks], Implies(assign(w, d), Not(And(assign(w, d), assign(w, d))))) ::: Each worker does no more than one task per day
ForAll([t1:tasks, t2:tasks], Implies(And(t1 == taping, t2 == priming), Not(And(Exists([d:tasks], assign(w, d)), Exists([d:tasks], assign(w, d))))) ::: Taping and priming are done on different days
ForAll([w:workers], ForAll([d:tasks], Implies(assign(w, d), Not(And(assign(w, d), assign(w, d))))) ::: Each worker does no more than one task per day

# Options
Question ::: Which one of the following could be a pair of members of the crew both of whom work on the same days as each other and each of whom perform two tasks?
is_sat(And(ForAll([t:tasks], assign(George, t) == assign(Maricita, t)), And(Count([t:tasks], assign(George, t)) == 2, Count([t:tasks], assign(Maricita, t)) == 2))) ::: (A)
is_sat(And(ForAll([t:tasks], assign(Helena, t) == assign(Kelly, t)), And(Count([t:tasks], assign(Helena, t)) == 2, Count([t:tasks], assign(Kelly, t)) == 2))) ::: (B)
is_sat(And(ForAll([t:tasks], assign(Inga, t) == assign(Leanda, t)), And(Count([t:tasks], assign(Inga, t)) == 2, Count([t:tasks], assign(Leanda, t)) == 2))) ::: (C)
is_sat(And(ForAll([t:tasks], assign(Kelly, t) == assign(Leanda, t)), And(Count([t:tasks], assign(Kelly, t)) == 2, Count([t:tasks], assign(Leanda, t)) == 2))) ::: (D)
is_sat(And(ForAll([t:tasks], assign(Leanda, t) == assign(Olaf, t)), And(Count([t:tasks], assign(Leanda, t)) == 2, Count([t:tasks], assign(Olaf, t)) == 2))) ::: (E)

question: If Guzman serves on the incentives committee, then which one of the following must be true?
options: A) Hawking serves on the finance committee.

E) Zhu serves on the finance committee.

members = EnumSort([Guzman, Hawking, Lepp, Miyauchi, Upchurch, Wharton, Zhu])

Any two of them are said to be sitting directly across from one another if and only if there are exactly three other people sitting between them, counting in either direction around the table. The following conditions apply: Fiona sits directly across from George. Harriet sits immediately next to neither Fiona nor Karl. Ingrid sits immediately next to, and immediately clockwise from, Olivia.
question: If Karl sits directly across from Harriet, then what is the minimum possible number of people sitting between George and Karl, counting clockwise from George to Karl?
options: A) zero
B) one
C) two
D) three
E) four

people = EnumSort([Fiona, George, Harriet, Ingrid, Karl, Manuel, Olivia, Peter])
positions = EnumSort([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8])
sits = Function([people] -> [positions])

# Constraints
ForAll([p:people], And(1 <= sits(p), sits(p) <= 8)) ::: each person sits at a unique position
ForAll([p:people], Distinct([p1:people, p2:people], sits(p1) != sits(p2))) ::: no two people sit at the same position

B) Jefferson is appointed to the appellate court.
C) Jefferson is appointed to the trial court.
D) Perkins is appointed to the appellate court.
E) Perkins is appointed to the trial court.
raw_logic_programs:
# Declarations
candidates = EnumSort([Hamadi, Jefferson, Kurtz, Li, McDonnell, Ortiz, Perkins])
courts = EnumSort([appellate, trial])
appointed_to = Function([candidates] -> [courts])

# Constraints
appointed_to(Li) == appellate ::: Li must be appointed to the appellate court
appointed_to(Kurtz) == trial ::: Kurtz must be appointed to the trial court
ForAll([c: candidates], Implies(appointed_to(c) == appellate, Not(appointed_to(Perkins) == appellate))) ::: Hamadi cannot be appointed to the same court as Perkins
appointed_to(Ortiz) == appellate ::: Ortiz is appointed to the appellate court

# Options
Question ::: If Ortiz is appointed to the appellate court, which one of the following must be true?
is_valid(ForAll([c: candidates], appointed_to(c) == appellate)) ::: (A)
is_valid(ForAll([c: candidates], appointed_to(c) == appellate)) ::: (B)
is_valid(ForAll([c: candidates], appointed_to(c) == trial)) ::: (C)
is_valid(appointed_to(Perkins) == appellate) ::: (D)
is_valid(appointed_to(Perkins) == trial) ::: (E)

context: Each of seven candidates for the position of judge—Hamadi, Jefferson, Kurtz, Li, McDonnell, Ortiz, and Perkins—will be appointed to an open position on one of two courts—the appellate court or the trial court. There are three open positions on the appellate court and six open positions on the trial court, but not all of them will be filled at this time. The judicial appointments will conform to the following conditions: Li must be appointed to the appellate court. Kurtz must be appointed to the trial court. Hamadi cannot be appointed to the same court as Perkins.
question: Which one of the following, if substituted for the condition that Hamadi cannot be appointed to the same court as Perkins, would have the same effect on the appointments of the seven candidates?
options: A) Hamadi and Perkins cannot both be appointed to the appellate court.
B) If Hamadi is not appointed to the trial court, then Perkins must be.
C) If Perkins is appointed to the same court as Jefferson, then Hamadi cannot be.
D) If Hamadi is appointed to the same court as Li, then Perkins must be appointed to the same court as Kurtz.
E) No three of Hamadi, Kurtz, Li, and Perkins can be appointed to the same court as each other.

question: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?
options: A) Fernando performs immediately before Juanita.
B) Ginny performs immediately before Hakim.
C) Hakim performs immediately before Ginny.
D) Juanita performs immediately before Ginny.
E) Kevin performs immediately before Hakim.

position = IntSort()
perform = Function([students] -> [position])

Distinct([s:students], perform(s)) ::: each position is unique
perform(Ginny) < perform(Fernando) ::: Ginny before Fernando
And(perform(Kevin) < perform(Hakim), perform(Kevin) < perform(Juanita)) ::: Kevin before Hakim and Juanita
Or(perform(Hakim) == perform(Fernando) + 1, perform(Fernando) == perform(Hakim) + 1) ::: Hakim adjacent to Fernando

is_exception(is_sat(perform(Juanita) + 1 == perform(Ginny))) ::: (D)
is_exception(is_sat(perform(Kevin) + 1 == perform(Hakim))) ::: (E)

context: A television programming director is scheduling a three-hour block of programs beginning at 1 P.M. The programs that are to fill this time block include an hour-long program called Generations and four half-hour programs: Roamin', Sundown, Terry, and Waterloo. The programs will be shown one after the other, each program shown exactly once. The schedule must meet the following constraints: Generations starts on the hour rather than the half hour. Terry starts on the half hour rather than the hour. Roamin' is shown earlier than Sundown. If Waterloo is shown earlier than Terry, it is shown immediately before Terry.
question: If Generations is the third program, then which one of the following could be true?
options: A) Roamin' is the second program.
B) Roamin' is the fifth program.
C) Sundown is the fourth program.
D) Terry is the fourth program.
E) Waterloo is the second program.
raw_logic_programs:
# Declarations
programs = EnumSort([Generations, Roamin, Sundown, Terry, Waterloo])
order = Function([programs] -> [int])
ForAll([p:programs], 1 <= order(p) <= 5)

# Constraints

question: If dish 6 is the only dish stored on the bottom shelf, which one of the following could be the list of dishes that are stored together on the middle shelf?

And(Count([d: dishes], shelf_position(d) == bottom) == 1, shelf_position(dish_6) == bottom) ::: dish 6 is the only dish on the bottom shelf

The first school to which juices are delivered must be the fourth one to which snacks are delivered.
question: If Isley is the first school to which snacks are delivered, which one of the following could be true?
options: A) Ferndale is the second school to which juices are delivered.
B) Hafford is the second school to which juices are delivered.
C) Hafford is the third school to which juices are delivered.
D) Isley is the first school to which juices are delivered.
E) Hafford is the second school to which snacks are delivered.

schools = EnumSort([Ferndale, Gladstone, Hafford, Isley])
juice_order = Function([schools] -> [int])
snack_order = Function([schools] -> [int])

ForAll([s: schools], 1 <= juice_order(s) <= 4) ::: each school has a juice delivery time
ForAll([s: schools], 1 <= snack_order(s) <= 4) ::: each school has a snack delivery time
Distinct([s: schools], juice_order(s)) ::: each juice delivery time is unique

is_valid(Exists([s: schools], juice_order(s) == 1 and s == Isley)) ::: (D)
is_valid(Exists([s: schools], snack_order(s) == 2 and s == Hafford)) ::: (E)

context: A record producer is planning the contents of a CD consisting of a sequence of exactly five instrumental pieces—Reciprocity, Salammbo, Trapezoid, Vancouver, and Wisteria. To create and sustain certain moods, the sequence of pieces will satisfy the following constraints: Salammbo must be earlier than Vancouver. Trapezoid must either be earlier than both Reciprocity and Salammbo or later than both Reciprocity and Salammbo. Wisteria must either be earlier than both Reciprocity and Trapezoid or later than both Reciprocity and Trapezoid.
question: If Wisteria is the first piece on the CD, then which one of the following CANNOT be true?
options: A) Trapezoid is the third piece on the CD.
B) Vancouver is the third piece on the CD.
C) Salammbo is the fourth piece on the CD.
D) Vancouver is the fourth piece on the CD
E) Trapezoid is the last piece on the CD.

pieces = EnumSort([Reciprocity, Salammbo, Trapezoid, Vancouver, Wisteria])
positions = IntSort()
opened = Function([pieces] -> [positions])

# Constraints
Distinct([p:pieces], opened(p)) ::: no two pieces have the same position
ForAll([p:pieces], And(1 <= opened(p), opened(p) <= 5)) ::: each position is between 1 and 5
opened(Salammbo) < opened(Vancouver) ::: Salammbo before Vancouver
And( (opened(Trapezoid) < opened(Reciprocity) ∧ opened(Trapezoid) < opened(Salammbo)) ∨ (opened(Trapezoid) > opened(Reciprocity) ∧ opened(Trapezoid) > opened(Salammbo)) ) ::: Trapezoid's condition
And( (opened(Wisteria) < opened(Reciprocity) ∧ opened(Wisteria) < opened(Trapezoid)) ∨ (opened(Wisteria) > opened(Reciprocity) ∧ opened(Wisteria) > opened(Trapezoid)) ) ::: Wisteria's condition
opened(Wisteria) == 1 ::: Wisteria is first

# Options

is_exception(is_sat(opened(Trapezoid) == 3)) ::: (A)
is_exception(is_sat(opened(Vancouver) == 3)) ::: (B)
is_exception(is_sat(opened(Salammbo) == 4)) ::: (C)
is_exception(is_sat(opened(Vancouver) == 4)) ::: (D)
is_exception(is_sat(opened(Trapezoid) == 5)) ::: (E)

E) Yoshida's and Zimmerman's

speakers = EnumSort([Long, Molina, Xiao, Yoshida, Zimmerman])
rooms = EnumSort([Gold, Rose])
times = EnumSort([1, 2, 3])

time = Function([speakers] -> [times])

# Constraints
ForAll([s:speakers], Exists([t:times], time(s) == t)) ::: Each speaker has a time
ForAll([s:speakers], Exists([r:rooms], room(s) == r)) ::: Each speaker has a room
ForAll([t:times], t == 1 => And(Count([s:speakers], And(time(s) == t, room(s) == Gold)) == 1, Count([s:speakers], And(time(s) == t, room(s) == Rose)) == 1)) ::: For time 1, each room has exactly one speech

ForAll([t:times], t == 3 => Count([s:speakers], time(s) == t) == 1) ::: For time 3, exactly one speech
And(time(Molina) < time(Long), room(Molina) == room(Long)) ::: Molina's speech is earlier than Long's and in the same room

context: A florist is filling a customer's order for three bouquets—bouquet 1, bouquet 2, and bouquet 3. Each of the bouquets is to be composed of one or more of five kinds of flowers—lilies, peonies, roses, snapdragons, and tulips—subject to the following conditions: Bouquets 1 and 3 cannot have any kind of flower in common. Bouquets 2 and 3 must have exactly two kinds of flowers in common. Bouquet 3 must have snapdragons. If a bouquet has lilies, that bouquet must also have roses but cannot have snapdragons. If a bouquet has tulips, that bouquet must also have peonies.
question: If lilies are in bouquet 1, which one of the following must
options: A) Lilies are in bouquet 2.
B) Peonies are in bouquet 3.
C) Roses are in bouquet 2.
D) Tulips are in bouquet 2.
E) Tulips are in bouquet 3.
raw_logic_programs:
# Declarations
flowers = EnumSort([lilies, peonies, roses, snapdragons, tulips])
bouquets = EnumSort([bouquet_1, bouquet_2, bouquet_3])
has = Function([bouquets, flowers] -> [bool])

# Constraints
ForAll([f:flowers], Not(And(has(bouquet_1, f), has(bouquet_3, f)))) ::: Bouquets 1 and 3 cannot have any kind of flower in common
ForAll([f:flowers], And(Implies(has(bouquet_2, f), has(bouquet_3, f)), Implies(has(bouquet_3, f), has(bouquet_2, f)))) ::: Bouquets 2 and 3 must have exactly two kinds of flowers in common
has(bouquet_3, snapdragons) ::: Bouquet 3 must have snapdragons
ForAll([b:bouquets], Implies(has(b, lilies), And(has(b, roses), Not(has(b, snapdragons)))) ::: If a bouquet has lilies, that bouquet must also have roses but cannot have snapdragons
ForAll([b:bouquets], Implies(has(b, tulips), has(b, peonies))) ::: If a bouquet has tulips, that bouquet must also have peonies

is_valid(ForAll([f:flowers], has(bouquet_2, f) == has(bouquet_3, f))) ::: (C)

B) Peonies and tulips are the only kinds of flowers in bouquet 1.
C) Lilies, peonies, and roses are the only kinds of flowers in bouquet 2.
D) Peonies, roses, and snapdragons are the only kinds of flowers in bouquet 2.
E) Peonies, snapdragons, and tulips are the only kinds of flowers in bouquet 3.
raw_logic_programs:
# Declarations
bouquets = EnumSort([bouquet1, bouquet2, bouquet3])
flowers = EnumSort([lilies, peonies, roses, snapdragons, tulips])
has = Function([bouquets, flowers] -> [bool])

# Constraints
ForAll([b: bouquets], Or(has(b, lilies), has(b, peonies), has(b, roses), has(b, snapdragons), has(b, tulips))) ::: each bouquet has at least one flower
ForAll([b: bouquets], Not(And(has(b, lilies), has(b, snapdragons)))) ::: if a bouquet has lilies, it cannot have snapdragons
ForAll([b: bouquets], Implies(has(b, lilies), And(has(b, roses), Not(has(b, snapdragons))))) ::: if a bouquet has lilies, it must have roses and cannot have snapdragons
ForAll([b: bouquets], Implies(has(b, tulips), has(b, peonies))) ::: if a bouquet has tulips, it must have peonies
ForAll([f: flowers], Not(And(has(bouquet1, f), has(bouquet3, f)))) ::: bouquets 1 and 3 cannot have any kind of flower in common
ForAll([f: flowers], And(Implies(has(bouquet2, f), has(bouquet3, f)), Implies(has(bouquet3, f), has(bouquet2, f)))) ::: bouquets 2 and 3 must have exactly two kinds of flowers in common
has(bouquet3, snapdragons) ::: bouquet 3 must have snapdragons

# Options
Question ::: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?
is_exception(is_sat(And(has(bouquet1, lilies), has(bouquet1, roses), Not(has(bouquet1, peonies)), Not(has(bouquet1, snapdragons)), Not(has(bouquet1, tulips))))) ::: (A)
is_exception(is_sat(And(has(bouquet1, peonies), has(bouquet1, tulips), Not(has(bouquet1, lilies)), Not(has(bouquet1, roses)), Not(has(bouquet1, snapdragons))))) ::: (B)
is_exception(is_sat(And(has(bouquet2, lilies), has(bouquet2, peonies), has(bouquet2, roses), Not(has(bouquet2, snapdragons)), Not(has(bouquet2, tulips))))) ::: (C)
is_exception(is_sat(And(has(bouquet2, peonies), has(bouquet2, roses), has(bouquet2, snapdragons), Not(has(bouquet2, lilies)), Not(has(bouquet2, tulips))))) ::: (D)
is_exception(is_sat(And(has(bouquet3, peonies), has(bouquet3, snapdragons), has(bouquet3, tulips), Not(has(bouquet3, lilies)), Not(has(bouquet3, roses))))) ::: (E)

context: A corporation's Human Resources department must determine annual bonuses for seven employees—Kimura, Lopez, Meng, and Peterson, who work in the Finance department; and Vaughan, Xavier, and Zane, who work in the Graphics department. Each employee will receive either a $1,000 bonus, a $3,000 bonus, or a $5,000 bonus, in accordance with the following: No one in the Graphics department receives a $1,000 bonus. Any employee who was rated Highly Effective receives a larger bonus than anyone in his or her department who was not rated Highly Effective. Only Lopez, Meng, and Xavier were rated Highly Effective.
question: Which one of the following is an allowable distribution of bonuses to the seven employees?
options: A) [Finance] Kimura: $1,000; Lopez: $5,000; Meng: $5,000; Peterson: $1,000 [Graphics] Vaughan: $3,000; Xavier: $3,000; Zane: $3,000
B) [Finance] Kimura: $1,000; Lopez: $5,000; Meng: $5,000; Peterson: $3,000 [Graphics] Vaughan: $3,000; Xavier: $5,000; Zane: $1,000
C) [Finance] Kimura: $1,000; Lopez: $5,000; Meng: $5,000; Peterson: $3,000 [Graphics] Vaughan: $3,000; Xavier: $5,000; Zane: $3,000
D) [Finance] Kimura: $3,000; Lopez: $5,000; Meng: $3,000; Peterson: $1,000 [Graphics] Vaughan: $3,000; Xavier: $5,000; Zane: $3,000
E) [Finance] Kimura: $3,000; Lopez: $5,000; Meng: $5,000; Peterson: $1,000 [Graphics] Vaughan: $1,000; Xavier: $5,000; Zane: $3,000
raw_logic_programs:
# Declarations
employees = EnumSort([Kimura, Lopez, Meng, Peterson, Vaughan, Xavier, Zane])
departments = EnumSort([Finance, Graphics])
bonuses = EnumSort([one_thousand, three_thousand, five_thousand])
bonus = Function([employees] -> [bonuses])

# Constraints
ForAll([e:employees], Implies(e in Graphics, bonus(e) != one_thousand)) ::: No one in the Graphics department receives a $1,000 bonus
ForAll([e:employees], Implies(bonus(e) == five_thousand, And(Implies(e in Finance, bonus(e) > bonus(OtherFinance)), Implies(e in Graphics, bonus(e) > bonus(OtherGraphics))))) ::: Any employee who was rated Highly Effective receives a larger bonus than anyone in his or her department who was not rated Highly Effective
ForAll([e:employees], Implies(And(e == Lopez, e == Meng, e == Xavier), bonus(e) == five_thousand)) ::: Only Lopez, Meng, and Xavier were rated Highly Effective

question: If only one of the employees receives a $1,000 bonus, which one of the following must be true?
options: A) Meng receives a $5,000 bonus.
B) Peterson receives a $3,000 bonus.
C) Meng receives a $3,000 bonus.
D) The employee who receives a $1,000 bonus is Peterson.
E) The employee who receives a $1,000 bonus is Kimura.

bonus = Function([employees] -> [Int])

ForAll([e:employees], ForAll([f:employees], Implies(And(Or(e == Lopez, e == Meng), Or(f == Kimura, f == Peterson), e != f), bonus(e) > bonus(f)))) ::: Any Highly Effective employee receives a larger bonus than anyone in their department who was not Highly Effective

ForAll([e:employees], Implies(Not(Or(e == Lopez, e == Meng, e == Xavier)), Not(Or(e == Lopez, e == Meng, e == Xavier)))) ::: Only Lopez, Meng, and Xavier were rated Highly Effective

is_valid(Implies(Count([e:employees], bonus(e) == 1) == 1, bonus(Kimura) == 1)) ::: (E)

context: A corporation's Human Resources department must determine annual bonuses for seven employees—Kimura, Lopez, Meng, and Peterson, who work in the Finance department; and Vaughan, Xavier, and Zane, who work in the Graphics department. Any employee who was rated Highly Effective receives a larger bonus than anyone in his or her department who was not rated Highly Effective. Only Lopez, Meng, and Xavier were rated Highly Effective.
question: Any of the following could be true of the seven employees EXCEPT:
options: A) The same number receive $1,000 bonuses as receive $3,000 bonuses.
B) More receive $1,000 bonuses than receive $3,000 bonuses.
C) The same number receive $1,000 bonuses as receive $5,000 bonuses.
D) More receive $1,000 bonuses than receive $5,000 bonuses.
E) More receive $3,000 bonuses than receive $5,000 bonuses.

# Declarations
employees = EnumSort([Kimura, Lopez, Meng, Peterson, Vaughan, Xavier, Zane])
bonus = Function([employees] -> [Int])

# Constraints
ForAll([e:employees], (e == Vaughan or e == Xavier or e == Zane) implies bonus(e) != 1) ::: No one in Graphics department receives a $1,000 bonus
ForAll([e:employees], (e == Kimura or e == Peterson) implies (bonus(e) < bonus(Lopez) and bonus(e) < bonus(Meng))) ::: Non-Highly Effective in Finance have less than Lopez and Meng
ForAll([e:employees], (e == Vaughan or e == Zane) implies bonus(e) < bonus(Xavier)) ::: Non-Highly Effective in Graphics have less than Xavier

is_exception(is_sat(Count([e:employees], bonus(e) == 1) == Count([e:employees], bonus(e) == 5))) ::: (C)
is_exception(is_sat(Count([e:employees], bonus(e) == 1) > Count([e:employees], bonus(e) == 5))) ::: (D)
is_exception(is_sat(Count([e:employees], bonus(e) == 3) > Count([e:employees], bonus(e) == 5))) ::: (E)

On each day except Saturday, there will be exactly one librarian on duty, with two on duty on Saturday, subject to the following constraints: Hill must be on desk duty earlier in the week than Leung. Kitson must be on desk duty earlier in the week than Zahn. Unless Leung is on desk duty on Saturday, Leung must be on desk duty earlier in the week than Flynn.

B) Only Flynn or Hill can be on desk duty on Monday.

E) Flynn must be on desk duty earlier in the week than both Moore and Zahn.

context: Each issue of a business newsletter has five slots, numbered 1 through 5. question: If, in a particular issue of the newsletter, slot 1 is occupied by the only industry feature in that issue, then which one of the following is required for that issue?
options: A) There is an industry feature that occupies slots 1 and 2, and only those slots.
B) There is an industry feature that occupies slots 1, 2, and 3, and only those slots.
C) There is a marketing feature that occupies slot 2 or slot 3 or both.
D) There is a marketing feature that occupies one or more of slots 2, 3, and 4.
E) There is a marketing feature that occupies slot 3 or slot 5 or both.

ForAll([s:slots], Or(is_feature(s), Not(is_feature(s)))) ::: Any slot not containing a feature contains a graphic
ForAll([s:slots], Implies(is_feature(s), Exists([f:features], occupied(s) == f))) ::: Each feature occupies one or more slots

occupied(1) == industry ::: Slot 1 is occupied by the only industry feature

Each entertainer will perform at one of six times—in the morning at 9:00 A.M., 10:00 A.M., or 11:00 A.M., or in the afternoon at 2:00 P.M., 3:00 P.M., or 4:00 P.M.—with no two entertainers performing at the same scheduled time. The order in which the entertainers perform is subject to the following constraints: Robinson must perform at some time before Zane. Yeaton's performance must be the next performance after Wu's. question: If Wu is scheduled to perform in the morning, then which one of the following could be true?
options: A) Robinson is scheduled to perform at 10:00 A.M.
B) Shahpari is scheduled to perform at 3:00 P.M.
C) Tigay is scheduled to perform at 2:00 P.M.
D) Yeaton is scheduled to perform at 3:00 P.M.
E) Zane is scheduled to perform at 11:00 A.M.

# Declarations
entertainers = EnumSort([Robinson, Shahpari, Tigay, Wu, Yeaton, Zane])
times = EnumSort([9, 10, 11, 2, 3, 4])
perform = Function([entertainers] -> [times])

# Constraints
Distinct([perform(e) for e in entertainers]) ::: no two entertainers perform at the same time
perform(Robinson) < perform(Zane) ::: Robinson must perform before Zane
ForAll([w:entertainers, y:entertainers], (w == Wu) implies (y == Yeaton) implies ( (perform(w) == 9 and perform(y) == 10) or (perform(w) == 10 and perform(y) == 11) or (perform(w) == 11 and perform(y) == 2) or (perform(w) == 2 and perform(y) == 3) or (perform(w) == 3 and perform(y) == 4) )) ::: Yeaton's performance is the next after Wu's
Or(perform(Tigay) == 2, perform(Tigay) == 3, perform(Tigay) == 4) ::: Tigay must perform in the afternoon
Or(perform(Zane) == 9, perform(Zane) == 10, perform(Zane) == 11) ::: Zane must perform in the morning
Or(perform(Wu) == 9, perform(Wu) == 10, perform(Wu) == 11) ::: Wu is scheduled to perform in the morning

# Options

is_sat(perform(Robinson) == 10) ::: (A)
is_sat(perform(Shahpari) == 3) ::: (B)
is_sat(perform(Tigay) == 2) ::: (C)
is_sat(perform(Yeaton) == 3) ::: (D)
is_sat(perform(Zane) == 11) ::: (E)

Each assistant will be assigned to exactly one course, and each course will have at least one assistant assigned to it. The assignment of assistants to courses is subject to the following conditions: Markets must have exactly two assistants assigned to it. Smith and Taj must be assigned to the same course as each other. Vogel and Yi cannot be assigned to the same course as each other. Yi and Zane must both be assigned to Pricing if either one of them is.
question: Which one of the following CANNOT be the complete assignment of assistants to Labor?
options: A) Ramos, Vogel
B) Ramos, Zane
C) Smith, Taj
D) Vogel, Zane
E) Yi, Zane

assistants = EnumSort([Ramos, Smith, Taj, Vogel, Yi, Zane])
courses = EnumSort([Labor, Markets, Pricing])
assign = Function([assistants] -> [courses])

# Constraints
Count([a:assistants], assign(a) == Markets) == 2 ::: Markets must have exactly two assistants
assign(Smith) == assign(Taj) ::: Smith and Taj must be assigned to the same course
assign(Vogel) != assign(Yi) ::: Vogel and Yi cannot be assigned to the same course
And(Implies(assign(Yi) == Pricing, assign(Zane) == Pricing), Implies(assign(Zane) == Pricing, assign(Yi) == Pricing)) ::: Yi and Zane must both be assigned to Pricing if either is
ForAll([c:courses], Count([a:assistants], assign(a) == c) >= 1) ::: Each course has at least one assistant

is_exception(is_sat(ForAll([a:assistants], And(Implies(assign(a) == Labor, Or(a == Ramos, a == Zane)), Implies(Or(a == Ramos, a == Zane), assign(a) == Labor))))) ::: (B)

is_exception(is_sat(ForAll([a:assistants], And(Implies(assign(a) == Labor, Or(a == Vogel, a == Zane)), Implies(Or(a == Vogel, a == Zane), assign(a) == Labor))))) ::: (D)

context: An economics department is assigning six teaching assistants—Ramos, Smith, Taj, Vogel, Yi, and Zane—to three courses—Labor, Markets, and Pricing. Each assistant will be assigned to exactly one course, and each course will have at least one assistant assigned to it. The assignment of assistants to courses is subject to the following conditions: Markets must have exactly two assistants assigned to it. Smith and Taj must be assigned to the same course as each other. Vogel and Yi cannot be assigned to the same course as each other. Yi and Zane must both be assigned to Pricing if either one of them is.
question: If Vogel is assigned to the same course as Zane, which one of the following CANNOT be true?
options: A) Ramos is assigned to Labor.
B) Smith is assigned to Labor.
C) Taj is assigned to Markets.
D) Ramos is assigned to Pricing.
E) Smith is assigned to Pricing.
raw_logic_programs:
# Declarations
technicians = EnumSort([Ramos, Smith, Taj, Vogel, Yi, Zane])
courses = EnumSort([Labor, Markets, Pricing])
assign = Function([technicians] -> [courses])

# Constraints
ForAll([t:technicians], assign(t) = Labor ∨ assign(t) = Markets ∨ assign(t) = Pricing) ::: Each assistant is assigned to exactly one course
Count([t:technicians], assign(t) = Markets) = 2 ::: Markets has exactly two assistants
assign(Smith) = assign(Taj) ::: Smith and Taj are in the same course
assign(Vogel) ≠ assign(Yi) ::: Vogel and Yi cannot be in the same course
Implies(assign(Yi) = Pricing, assign(Zane) = Pricing) ∧ Implies(assign(Zane) = Pricing, assign(Yi) = Pricing) ::: Yi and Zane must both be in Pricing if either is
assign(Vogel) = assign(Zane) ::: Vogel is assigned to the same course as Zane

# Options
Question ::: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?
is_exception(is_sat(assign(Taj) = Markets)) ::: (C)
